title: Tokenization & Word Embeddings
description: Convert raw text strings to vector representations. Compare One-Hot, TF-IDF, Word2Vec, GloVe, and subword tokenization (BPE).

slides.title: From Strings to Continuous Vectors 🔡
slides.content:
# The Evolution of Text Representation

Computers cannot compute derivatives on raw characters. Text must be parsed into integer **tokens** and mapped into continuous geometric vector space.

| Representation Technique | Dimensionality | Semantic Awareness | Sparsity |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **One-Hot Encoding** | Vocabulary size $V$ ($50,000+$) | Zero (all words are orthogonal unit vectors) | Extremely Sparse (99.99% zeros) |
| **TF-IDF** | Vocabulary size $V$ | Frequency-based word importance | Sparse |
| **Word2Vec / GloVe** | Dense low-dimensional ($100-300$) | High (geometric vector arithmetic: King - Man + Woman = Queen) | Dense Continuous |
| **Contextual (BERT/GPT)** | $768 - 4096+$ | Deeply contextual (resolves polysemy: river "bank" vs money "bank") | Dense Continuous |

quizData.question: What is the critical advantage of dense word embeddings (like Word2Vec) over One-Hot vectors?

options.text: They assign every word an integer between 0 and 9
They capture semantic similarity as geometric proximity in continuous vector space
They eliminate the need for GPU hardware

quizData.explanation: Word embeddings map semantically similar words (e.g. 'doctor' and 'physician') to vectors that have high cosine similarity in continuous space.

slides.title: Subword Tokenization: BPE & WordPiece 🧩
slides.content:
# Conquering Out-of-Vocabulary (OOV) Words

Early NLP tokenized on whitespace. If a user typed a rare word like "unhappiness", the model output an `[UNK]` (Unknown) token.

Modern models (GPT, Claude, LLaMA) use **Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE)**:

* Starts at character level: `u, n, h, a, p, p, i, n, e, s, s`
* Iteratively merges the most frequent adjacent character pairs into subwords: `un`, `happi`, `ness`
* Any word—even typos or foreign terms—can be broken down into familiar subword constituents!

slides.title: Vector Similarity in Python 🐍
slides.content: Computing cosine similarity between dense semantic vectors:
slides.codeSnippet:
import numpy as np

def cosine_similarity(v1, v2):
    return np.dot(v1, v2) / (np.linalg.norm(v1) * np.linalg.norm(v2))

# Hypothetical 3D embeddings [Royalty, Femininity, Technology]
king  = np.array([0.9, 0.1, 0.0])
queen = np.array([0.9, 0.8, 0.0])
apple = np.array([0.1, 0.0, 0.9])

print('Similarity (King, Queen):', round(cosine_similarity(king, queen), 3))
print('Similarity (King, Apple):', round(cosine_similarity(king, apple), 3))

slides.title: AI Pro Tip: Token Counts 💡
slides.content:
## Rule of Thumb: Tokens vs Words
In modern English LLMs using BPE, 1,000 tokens corresponds to approximately **750 words** (roughly 4 characters per token). Keep this ratio in mind when estimating API token costs!
